Article.ArticleTitle: Defining a cohort of men who may not require repeat prostate biopsy based on PCA3 score and MRI: The dual negative effect.

Abstract.AbstractText: Prostate Cancer (PCa) overdiagnosis and overtreatment is a concern for clinicians and policy makers. Multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and the PCA3 urine test select for clinically significant cases. We explore how well the tests perform in combination for men with previous biopsies.

We collected clinicopathologic data from all patients with a PCA3 test from 2011 to June 2016 in accordance with ethics committee approval. This included patients on active surveillance (AS) for low-risk PCa and those without PCa with previous negative biopsies and suspicion of occult disease. We explored whether age, PSA, PCA3 score, mpMRI, DRE, family history and prostate size predicted for clinically significant prostate cancer on repeat biopsy. Negative predictive value (NPV) of mpMRI and PCA3 score were calculated.

470 patients were included and PCA3 score was abnormal (≥35) in 32.5% of cases. In the multivariate model with 154 men, only age (OR 1.08, 95%CI 1.01-1.16), mpMRI PI-RADS score 4 (OR 16.6, 95%CI 3.9-70.0) or 5 (OR 28.3, 95%CI 5.7-138), and PCA3 score (OR 2.9, 95%CI 1.0-8.8) predicted for clinically significant cancer on biopsy. No patients with a negative mpMRI and normal PCA3 score had clinically significant PCa on biopsy (100% NPV p<0.0001).

In patients with dual negative tests (mpMRI and PCA3 score), clinically significant PCa was never found on biopsy, which may be unnecessary in this group. This study is limited by its retrospective design, selection bias and lack of cost-effectiveness data.
